_note: Italian tongue twisters (scioglilingua) for /tongue-twisters. The well-known ones are traditional folk rhymes passed on orally (Trentatré trentini, Sopra la panca, Apelle figlio di Apollo, Tre tigri, Se oggi seren non è, the arcivescovo); the shorter lines are practice lines written for this course around one sound, and the hint says so. Each one is first read out (slowly, then at speed), then the learner repeats it and gets points per word, the same scoring as /pronunciation-check. focus: sound ids from src/lib/ausspracheTipps.js. hint: what the twister means, in simple English. Ids are the old slot ids (content-plan §1.3), so they no longer describe the text; this set has 15 (quality over quantity). `audio` is set to true once public/audio/zungenbrecher/<id>-langsam.mp3 and <id>.mp3 exist; until then the browser voice (it-IT) reads them. mini (optional): an animal in the twister, so a small Mini-Crew sticker (src/lib/minis.js) sits on the card. mascot (optional): the same with an animal of the crew. dialect (optional): the same twister in a regional accent, voiced as <id>-<slug(dialect.name)>.mp3, only for listening and never scored; none in this set.

sentences.hint: Three tigers against three tigers. A very old short twister: the tr at the start of tre and tigri needs a quick, clean r.

sentences.text: Anna ama la nonna e la nonna ama Anna.
sentences.hint: Anna loves her grandmother and her grandmother loves Anna. A practice line: the nn in Anna and nonna is long, the n in ama is short.

sentences.text: Ha fame, ha sete e ha sonno: ha tutto, ma non ha tempo.
sentences.hint: He has hunger, thirst and sleepiness: he has everything, but no time. A practice line: the h of ha is always silent; the tt of tutto is long.

sentences.text: Cecilia cucina ceci con cipolle e ciliegie.
sentences.hint: Cecilia cooks chickpeas with onions and cherries. A practice line: ce and ci are “che” and “chi” as in “church”; cu is hard.

sentences.text: Gli gnomi mangiano gli gnocchi ogni giorno.
sentences.hint: The gnomes eat gnocchi every day. A practice line: gli is one sound, and so is gn.

sentences.text: Lo zio mangia la pizza e la zia beve il tè con lo zucchero.
sentences.hint: The uncle eats pizza and the aunt drinks tea with sugar. A practice line: five z sounds, each a ts or dz, never a buzz.

sentences.text: Sopra la panca la capra campa, sotto la panca la capra crepa.
sentences.hint: On the bench the goat lives, under the bench the goat dies. A traditional twister: campa and crepa differ in one sound. No puff of air on p and c.

sentences.text: Sul tagliere l'aglio taglia, non tagliare la tovaglia.
sentences.hint: Cut the garlic on the board, don't cut the tablecloth. A traditional-style twister built on gli: tagliere, aglio, taglia, tagliare, tovaglia.

sentences.text: Trentatré trentini entrarono a Trento, tutti e trentatré trotterellando.
sentences.hint: Thirty-three people from Trento came into Trento, all thirty-three trotting along. The most famous Italian twister. Keep the stress on the é of trentatré and on the long tt.
Rosa nibbles a red beet. A practice line: r at the start of a word is a trill, ss in rossa is long.

sentences.text: Quel quadro quasi quadrato quest'anno costa quattrocento euro.
sentences.hint: That nearly square picture costs four hundred euros this year. A practice line: every qu is /kw/, you say the u.

sentences.text: Lo sciatore lascia la sciarpa sulla scia della scuola di sci.
sentences.hint: The skier leaves his scarf on the trail of the ski school. A practice line: sci and sce are /ʃ/, scu and sca are /sk/.

sentences.text: Apelle, figlio di Apollo, fece una palla di pelle di pollo, e tutti i pesci vennero a galla per vedere la palla di pelle di pollo fatta da Apelle, figlio di Apollo.
sentences.hint: Apelle, son of Apollo, made a ball out of chicken skin, and all the fish came to the surface to see the ball of chicken skin made by Apelle, son of Apollo. A traditional rhyme: p, ll and the gli of figlio all together.

sentences.text: Se oggi seren non è, doman seren sarà; se non sarà seren, si rasserenerà.
sentences.hint: If today is not fine, tomorrow will be fine; if it is not fine, it will clear up. An old weather saying, with the old short forms seren and doman.

sentences.text: Se l'arcivescovo di Costantinopoli si disarcivescoviscostantinopolizzasse, tu ti disarcivescoviscostantinopolizzeresti?
sentences.hint: If the archbishop of Constantinople were to stop being archbishop of Constantinople, would you stop too? An invented, very long word, famous as a challenge. Take it slowly, one syllable at a time.
